dialogue.speaker: Michael
dialogue.text: The giáo dục system in Vietnam is very different from America. Students here học many more hours, but I'm not sure they actually learn more.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: You nghĩ so? In Russia, we also học for many hours. I nghĩ serious giáo dục creates disciplined people. Maybe that's why Russians are good at chess. My old teacher used to say that giáo dục is the key to success.

dialogue.speaker: Michael
dialogue.text: But giáo dục isn't just about cramming knowledge. When I was in America, we were encouraged to think creatively. I once had a very inspiring teacher who taught us that real giáo dục is about asking questions, not just memorization.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Hmm... that's interesting. My ex-boyfriend also used to talk about "creative thinking" like that. But in the end, he couldn't solve a simple math problem. I nghĩ giáo dục needs to balance discipline and creativity, don't you think?

dialogue.speaker: Michael
dialogue.text: Ex-boyfriend? I didn't know you had... Oh, it's fine. About giáo dục, I agree that balance is needed. But I nghĩ in Vietnam, they focus too much on grades and forget the real meaning of học.
